status_summary: Executive Order 14421, signed 2026-08-26 and published 2026-08-31, declares a national emergency to secure the bulk-power system and authorizes the Energy Secretary to prohibit or condition transactions in foreign-produced grid equipment linked to covered foreign entities, including equipment already installed. It directs DOE to publish implementing rules as needed within 120 days, about 2026-12-24. A law firm summary describes it as building on and expanding the 2020 order, though it labels the order 14420; the Federal Register gives 14421. Earlier, Executive Order 14262 (published 2025-04-14) addressed grid reliability through emergency orders. On structure, the 2025-11-20 DOE chart leaves CESER a separate office, and a new head named in July 2026 holds the title Director, not Assistant Secretary.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14262 on grid reliability and security (signed 2025-04-08) published; it directs faster use of Federal Power Act 202(c) emergency orders and a reserve margin methodology, and does not address foreign equipment.
DOE published a reorganization chart; CESER was among the offices left unchanged.
Trade press reported DOE named a new Director of CESER; the title is Director, not Assistant Secretary.

Executive Order 14421 signed, declaring a national emergency to secure the bulk-power system and authorizing the Energy Secretary to prohibit or condition foreign-produced grid equipment; published 2026-08-31.
